### 1. Scene
A plate of sliced cooked meat, probably pork, with leafy salad, broccoli, cauliflower, and a few bacon-like strips.

### 2. Vessel
A large white dinner plate, approximately **27 cm** across. Its edges are partly cropped.
Area ≈ 3.14 × 13.5² = **572 cm²**.

### 3–7. Items, area, volume, weight, and energy
Area shares below are non-overlapping estimates. The glossy leaves suggest a small amount of oily dressing.

| Visible item | Plate area | Area × height = gross volume | Bulk density | Weight | kcal/100 g | kcal |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Cooked meat, likely pork | 25% | 143 × 1.3 = 186 ml | 0.94 | 175 g | 250 | 438 |
| Lettuce and spinach | 34% | 194 × 2.7 = 524 ml | 0.15 | 79 g | 20 | 16 |
| Broccoli | 12% | 69 × 2 = 138 ml | 0.60 | 83 g | 35 | 29 |
| Cauliflower | 5% | 29 × 1.7 = 49 ml | 0.60 | 29 g | 25 | 7 |
| Bacon-like strips | 3% | 17 × 1.1 = 19 ml | 0.95 | 18 g | 500 | 90 |
| Small carrot, onion, raisin/cranberry pieces | 3% | 17 × 1.2 = 20 ml | 0.70 | 14 g | 140 | 20 |
| Oily dressing | On leaves* | Approximately 10 ml | 1.0 | 10 g | 880 | 88 |

*Dressing overlaps the salad rather than occupying additional plate area. Food coverage totals **82%**.

### 8. Sanity check
The estimate is **408 g and approximately 688 kcal**, plausible for a mostly covered dinner plate with substantial meat and airy greens. Meat identity and dressing quantity are the largest uncertainties.
